title: Sandy Beaches in Tučepi: Where Real Sand Is (2027)
metaDescription: Tučepi has no true sand beach: Kamena, Slatina and Jadran are fine pebble. Nearest sand-mix and real sand beaches, with surfaces, shade and travel times.
content:
## Does Tučepi have a sandy beach?

No. Tučepi has no true sandy beach, and neither does the rest of the Makarska Riviera. The town's beaches are fine pebble, with concrete or rock sunbathing platforms in places. The coast stretches roughly 4 km and is often described as the longest beach on the Riviera. It is built from linked sections, not one continuous cove. Visitors who want real sand have to drive to Omiš or Split, or settle for a sand-and-pebble mix in Podgora or Zaostrog.

## Beach surfaces in Tučepi

The pebbles here are small and rounded, and easy to walk on barefoot. The sea stays clear because waves do not stir up sand. The sections are:

### Kamena (fine pebble)
Kamena is the longest section and lies along the coastal promenade. The entry is gradual, so small children can wade a good distance before the water reaches waist height. Pines and tamarisks line the promenade and give decent natural shade, mostly at the back of the beach. It is busy in July and August but has space to spread out. Parking is easier here than in Makarska. Park along the roads behind the promenade or in the paid lots near the centre, and arrive before 9:00 in peak season.

### Slatina, Ratac and Kraj (fine pebble)
These neighbouring sections run on from Kamena. They have the same fine pebble and shallow entry, with water attractions such as pedal boats and slides in season. Shade is mixed: pine cover in some parts, bare sun in others.

### Jadran and Lučica (fine pebble and concrete)
These sit in the centre of town beside the hotels and the main cluster of cafés. The pebble is fine and the entry mild. Concrete platforms and loungers take up part of the shoreline, and natural shade is limited. These are the most crowded stretches. Parking is possible nearby but fills up by mid-morning in summer.

All of Tučepi's beaches can be reached on foot from the centre. From Makarska the walk is about 3 km along the coastal path, or take the local bus.

## Nearest beaches with sand or a sandy seabed

### Plišivac, Podgora (about 6 km)
Plišivac has fine pebble over a sandy seabed. That makes it the softest underfoot of the nearby options. It lies on the walking route from Podgora, with two smaller beaches before it. Shade is partial and crowds are moderate. Park in Podgora and walk. It is a 10-minute drive from Tučepi.

### Zaostrog (about 30 km south)
Zaostrog has pebble beaches with some sand and a quiet, village-scale atmosphere. The entry is gentle. Crowds are far lighter than in Tučepi and parking is simple along the village front. Allow about 30 minutes by car on the coastal road.

### Omiš (about 60 km north, 50 minutes)
The sandy beach at Omiš runs for more than 1 km and is very shallow, so children can walk a long way out. This is the nearest option where sand is the main surface, and it mixes with fine gravel in places. Shade is limited and the river mouth can make the water cooler and less clear. Drive the coast road north, or take the regular coach from Makarska.

### Bačvice, Split (about 85 km, 1 hour 15 minutes)
Bačvice is a genuinely sandy city beach with very shallow water. Its sand is the main draw, but it is crowded, has little shade, and is surrounded by concrete promenades and bars. Parking in Split is difficult and paid. A day trip is realistic only if sand matters more than a quiet beach.

## What about Punta Rata and Nugal?

Punta Rata in Brela is often called sandy but is fine white pebble under pines. Nugal, between Makarska and Tučepi, is a pebble cove reached on foot. Neither counts as sand.

## Local tips

- Pack water shoes for the rock and concrete edges, not for the fine pebble.
- Go before 9:00 or after 17:00 for space on the central sections. Kamena has the most room.
- Spread a thick beach mat. Fine pebble is comfortable to lie on, but a mat keeps your towel clean.
- Base the sand trip around Omiš. Combine it with the Cetina river canyon, because it is too far for a short swim.

## Verdict: is Tučepi right for people who want sand?

Not if sand is the priority. Do not drive 85 km to Bačvice for one afternoon on a crowded city beach when Kamena is a calm, shallow, shaded fine-pebble strip a few minutes from your door. Children manage well here because the entry is gentle, and the water is clearer than at sandy beaches. Tučepi suits families and relaxed swimmers who accept pebble. For people who want true sand every day, Omiš is the better base, with Podgora's Plišivac as the nearest softer compromise.

faq.question: Is there a sandy beach in Tučepi?
faq.answer: No. Tučepi's beaches are fine pebble, with some concrete platforms. The Makarska Riviera has no true sand beach, only pebble beaches with a sandy seabed in places.

faq.question: Are Tučepi beaches good for small children?
faq.answer: Yes. Kamena, Slatina and Jadran have a gentle, shallow entry and fine pebble. Kamena also has pine shade and easy parking compared with Makarska.

faq.question: Where is the nearest real sandy beach to Tučepi?
faq.answer: The nearest beach where sand is the main surface is in Omiš, about 60 km and 50 minutes away. Bačvice in Split is also sandy, about 85 km and 1 hour 15 minutes away.

faq.question: Is Punta Rata in Brela a sandy beach?
faq.answer: No. Punta Rata is fine white pebble under pine trees, though it is often described as sandy. It has a gentle entry that suits families.

faq.question: Which beach near Tučepi has the softest seabed?
faq.answer: Plišivac in Podgora, about 6 km away, has fine pebble over a sandy seabed. It is the nearest softer-feeling beach and takes about 10 minutes by car.

faq.question: Is parking easy at Tučepi beaches?
faq.answer: Parking is easier than in Makarska, with spaces on the streets behind the promenade. Central lots near Jadran and Lučica fill by mid-morning in July and August, so arrive early.

quickAnswer: Tučepi has no true sandy beach. Its long coast is fine pebble with a gentle, shallow entry that suits children. The nearest sand-and-pebble mix is Plišivac in Podgora (about 6 km). Real sand is farther away: Omiš (about 60 km, 50 minutes) and Bačvice in Split (about 85 km, 1 hour 15 minutes).
